Doppler

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows the line-of-sight velocity component that changes the received carrier frequency.

Instantaneous range rate is the projection of relative velocity onto the line from receiver to transmitter: ṙ = vrelative · r̂. Positive range rate means recession.

At speeds much smaller than light speed, Δf ≈ −fcṙ/c. Recession lowers received frequency, while approach raises it. Transverse motion contributes no first-order shift at that instant.

A large inertial orbital speed can coexist with a small Earth-station range rate. The reference frame and line-of-sight projection must be specified before interpreting a speed as Doppler.

Example

At a 1 GHz carrier, recession at 300 m/s gives approximately −1 kHz Doppler when c is rounded to 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

Model and course sources

    Practice

    1. At one instant, a spacecraft's relative velocity is perpendicular to its line of sight. What first-order Doppler shift does this model predict?

    Evaluate the dot product before using the speed magnitude.

    Zero at that instant, because the range rate is zero. Its direction can change later, producing a nonzero range rate and Doppler shift.
